citazioni: Variable-temperature data collection reveals an order-disorder phase transition between AIIα and AIIβ (Supplementary Fig. 6).

Upon cooling to 100 K, the same crystal undergoes a significant structural transformation, characterized by marked destruction of the monoclinic symmetry and appearance of triclinic twin domains in the diffraction pattern (Fig. 2b) (Supplementary Fig. 12).

To examine the PT behavior at various temperatures, ϕ-scan data was collected over a temperature range from 298 K to 120 K. Initially, a 20 K decrement was applied during the transition from 298 to 220 K, followed by 10 K intervals between 220 and 120 K.
Notable shifts in the lattice parameters (a, b, c) and unit cell angles (α, β, γ) and volume in the vicinity of ~190 K clearly indicate a PT (Fig. 5a).
AIIα undergoes non-merohedral twinning during an enantiotropic SCSC phase transition to AIIβ at temperatures equal to or below 198 K.

The enantiotropic transition was characterized as an order-disorder phase transition in DMSO solvent, which resulted in conversion of AIIα to AIIβ, and was observed at Tc~199 K through variable-temperature SCXRD and low-temperature DSC.
Phi-scans were recorded between 298 K to 110 K in 10 K intervals, with cooling and heating controlled at 1 K per minute via an Oxford Cryo-stream.
Notably, a martensitic phase transition occurs between AIIα ↔ AIIβ, driven by complete rotational disorder of the DMSO molecules.
This structural adaptability creates sufficient space for the DMSO solvent to adopt an ordered conformation in the crystal structure below the phase transition temperature.
The driving force for the order-disorder PT is due to the increase in configurational entropy, whose magnitude is Rln2 = 5.76 J mol−1 K−133,44–46.

gruppi_coinvolti.citazione: Variable-temperature SCXRD reveals a gradual shift in the occupancy ratio (Fig. 3c) of the DMSO configurations from 0.818(2):0.182(2) at 298 K to 0.954(2):0.046(2) at 200 K.

gruppi_coinvolti.gruppo: DMSO solvent molecules (fully ordered in AIIβ)
gruppi_coinvolti.citazione: However, following the PT, the DMSO becomes fully ordered in the AIIβ phase (Fig. 3b).
Since the solvent molecule ordering drives the phase transition, halogen-substituted benzimidamide interactions remain largely unchanged.

Similar to AIIα, tetramers (Supplementary Fig. 13a) are formed through N2-H4A…O2, N2-H4B…O2 hydrogen bonds and additionally supported by S1…C9, S2…C22, and C23-H23…C2(π)/C3(π) interactions, enhancing structural stability.

At 298 K, these weak intermolecular Cl…Cl interactions span a distance of 3.627 Å, which exceeds the sum of the vdW radii (Fig. 6a). As the temperature decreases to 200 K, the distance contracts to 3.551 Å (Fig. 6b), and after the phase transition at 100 K, it further shortens to 3.437 Å (Fig. 6c).
The results indicate that all the molecules remained invariant throughout the process of the PT of AIIα ↔ AIIβ.

eventi.conflitto: Temperatura di transizione: «in the vicinity of ~190 K» (parametri di cella, Fig. 5a, Risultati), «equal to or below 198 K» (Metodi), «Tc~199 K» (abstract, introduzione; e' la T del DSC in riscaldamento). Per il raffreddamento con la SCXRD si tiene ~190 K (Risultati, il passo in cui il cristallo e' gemellato); le altre sono nei campi di citazione.
eventi.note: Transizione ordine-disordine del solo DMSO (SCSC, geminazione pseudo-meroedrica) da AIIα monoclina P21/n a AIIβ triclina P-1 (4 molecole nell'unita' asimmetrica): a 220 K un solo dominio, a 160 K domini gemellati. Passi di 20 K da 298 a 220 K e di 10 K da 220 a 120 K (Risultati); i Metodi dicono 298-110 K a passi di 10 K con 1 K al minuto. L'occupanza del DMSO va da 0.818:0.182 a 298 K a 0.954:0.046 a 200 K (ordinamento graduale, che spiega l'assenza di picco DSC). Variazioni di cella: ΔV −4.59%; la distanza Cl···Cl scende da 3.627 Å (298 K) a 3.551 Å (200 K) a 3.437 Å (100 K) e lascia spazio al DMSO ordinato. Forza motrice: entropia configurazionale, Rln2 = 5.76 J mol−1 K−1. DSC in raffreddamento da 298 a 120 K a 1 K min−1: nessun evento termico rilevato («could not be detected under these conditions»), quindi nessun evento DSC negativo.

citazioni: Upon heating from the cooled state, a pronounced endothermic phase transition was detected at Tcycle 1 = 199.35 K. This transition corresponds to the conversion of AIIβ back to AIIα phase, accompanied by an enthalpy change of 1.213 J g−1 (Fig. 2c).

The continuation of the DSC experiments for the second and third cycles yielded highly consistent results. The transition temperature remained close to the initial value at Tcycle 2 = 199.10 K and Tcycle 3 = 199.30 K in the second and third cycles, while the associated enthalpy changes were 2.367 J g−1 and 1.161 J g−1, respectively (Fig. 2c).
During the first cooling-heating cycle, crystals of the AIIα phase were cooled from room temperature (298 K) to 120 K at a slow rate of 1 K min−1.
Variable-temperature SCXRD measurements confirmed that the phase transition is fully reversible, with the formation of the parent phase AIIα after heating.

On the other hand, during heating, the crystal transforms from a completely ordered AIIβ to a disordered AIIα structure, showing the sharp co-operative nature of the transition marked by the endotherm during consecutive cycles.

Low-temperature DSC was carried out on a NETZSCH 3500 Sirius, scanning from 30 °C to −170 °C with liquid nitrogen cooling and a nitrogen purge of 20 mlmin-1. A 19 mg sample was cycled at 1 Kmin-1 with a 2-min isothermal hold at 170 °C and 30 °C.

The enantiotropic transition was characterized as an order-disorder phase transition in DMSO solvent, which resulted in conversion of AIIα to AIIβ, and was observed at Tc~199 K through variable-temperature SCXRD and low-temperature DSC.

Il testo dice che la SCXRD a temperatura variabile conferma la reversibilita' completa con AIIα dopo il riscaldamento (Fig. 3c: occupanza da 298 a 100 K e ritorno a 298 K); senza una T propria, e' lo stesso evento. Il campione di DSC e' «crystals of the AIIα phase» (19 mg). L'entalpia del ciclo 2 e' piu' del doppio degli altri.

citazioni: When block crystals were submerged in SO, the growth of needle-like crystals began within 20 min, and this transformation continued until complete conversion into the second form occurred after 24 h. SCXRD analysis of the newly formed needle-shaped crystals confirmed the generation of AI and BI polymorphs (Fig. 7).
To explore polymorphic interconversion at room temperature, temporal microscopic imaging and thermal characterization were employed to assess the stability profile of the crystals.
However, immersing crystals of AIIα and BII in silicone oil triggered conversion to AI and BI crystals, completing the transition within 24 h, as confirmed by SCXRD studies.

A distinct phase transition is observed when single crystals of AIIα and BII are immersed in SO, transforming into AI and BI, respectively. This transformation follows a nucleation and growth mechanism, where the daughter phase (AI and BI) originates from the parent crystals (AIIα and BII).
An intriguing SCSC phase transition was observed in the presence of silicone oil (SO).

Upon exposure to external stimuli, such as heat or SO, the AIIα and BII crystals undergo solvent loss (DMSO), which induces a reorganization into energetically more favorable supramolecular motifs, thereby transitioning into AI and BI.
Needle-like crystals began to emerge from the block crystals of AIIα and BII, indicating a rapid transformation (Fig. 7).
The interaction with SO begins at the crystal surface, wherein the progression of the AI/BI phase boundary on the surface of crystals of AIIα/BII is clearly visible in optical images (Fig. 7).

gruppi_coinvolti.citazione: It may be postulated that this transformation is driven by possible supramolecular interactions, involving the oxygen atom in DMSO and the hydrophobic chlorophenyl/bromophenyl moiety in compound A/B with the silicon atoms in silicone oil (Fig. 12a, b), which may facilitate the elimination of DMSO solvent and the conversion of the resulting solid into more stable forms, namely AI and BI, respectively.

eventi.note: Cristalli a blocco immersi in olio di silicone: dopo 20 min iniziano a crescere cristalli aghiformi e dopo 24 h la conversione e' completa (Fig. 7); l'interazione parte dalla superficie e il fronte AI/BI avanza sul cristallo madre. Il testo dice «SCSC» nel titolo della sezione e nel testo, e «nucleation and growth» nelle Conclusioni. Il fenomeno compare gia' al montaggio dei cristalli per la SCXRD (l'olio e' usato come olio crioprotettivo) e anche con una goccia di olio in laboratorio. Via scelta solvente/sospensione (immersione in un liquido); la perdita di DMSO e' dichiarata («solvent loss (DMSO)») ma l'olio non e' ne' vuoto ne' aria. Il testo propone (con «may») interazioni fra l'ossigeno del DMSO e il gruppo fenile idrofobo con il silicio dell'olio. Stesso fenomeno per la serie bromurata (E4).

citazioni: Variable-temperature data collection indicates that no phase transition was observed during the temperature variation from 298 to 100 K.
In contrast, the BII crystal exhibited a steady, linear change in the unit cell parameters across the same temperature range (Supplementary Table 8), indicating the absence of any PT (Fig. 5b).

In contrast, the BII crystalline phase features shorter Br…Br interactions. At 298 K, the Br…Br distance is 3.706 Å (Fig. 6a), which is nearly equal to twice the vdW radii. This distance decreases to 3.649 Å (Fig. 6b) at 200 K and further reduces to 3.601 Å (Fig. 6c) near 100 K.

The continued presence of DMSO disorder at lower temperature (down to 100 K) in BII is attributed to the absence of sufficient free volume, which prevents complete reordering of the solvent molecules.

citazioni: Images captured during heating show the pristine AIIα crystals (image 1 in Fig. 8d) begin to undergo desolvation of DMSO solvent after 50 °C (image 2 in Fig. 8d).
As the temperature rises, desolvation increases slowly, leading to the emergence of an unidentified phase, following minor solvent loss (image 3–6 in Fig. 8d).
TGA analysis supports this interpretation, indicating a 2.049% weight loss, corresponding to the loss of DMSO solvent, between a temperature range of 50 °C to 105 °C (Fig. 8c).

The DSC trace begins with a broad endothermic peak starting around 50 °C, followed by a minor endothermic peak at 88 °C (ΔH = 0.83 J g−1), highlighted by a green circle, and then a major melting peak at 96 °C (ΔH = 74.03 J g−1) (Fig. 8a).

DSC was performed on a Perkin-Elmer DSC 6000 from 25 °C to 200 °C under nitrogen, using bulk powder and polymorphs of A and B at a scan rate of 1 and 5 °C min−1. Samples were sealed in covered aluminum pans, and heat flow was recorded as a function of temperature.
Heating was applied from 20 to 200 °C at a constant rate of 1 °C min−1.

In contrast, AIIα displays a more complex and multiphase thermal response due to residual DMSO, which initiates desolvation upon heating and facilitates the transformation into an intermediate phase that ultimately resembles AI.

citazioni: The variable-temperature SCXRD data were sufficient to confirm that the AIIα crystal exhibited multiple domains at an elevated temperature of 362 K. Upon thermal treatment, these domains transitioned into a second polymorphic form, corresponding to AI (Supplementary Fig. 26).

In contrast, AIIα displays a more complex and multiphase thermal response due to residual DMSO, which initiates desolvation upon heating and facilitates the transformation into an intermediate phase that ultimately resembles AI.
Overall, the combined thermal analysis (DSC, TGA, HSM, and SCXRD) reveals that polymorphs AI and AIIα possess distinct thermal behaviors.

Upon exposure to external stimuli, such as heat or SO, the AIIα and BII crystals undergo solvent loss (DMSO), which induces a reorganization into energetically more favorable supramolecular motifs, thereby transitioning into AI and BI.

citazioni: HSM observations support this conclusion, desolvation begins as the temperature rises (Fig. 9c), followed by nucleation and growth of BI crystals around 108 °C, highlighted in a green box (Fig. 9c), which melt at 114 °C, consistent with DSC findings.

TGA analysis confirms that BII initially contains 20.004% DMSO solvent. By 150 °C, approximately 11.765% of this content is lost, indicating that some solvent remains during the cooling cycle (Fig. 9b).

Meanwhile, the isomorphous polymorph BII (red) exhibits a DSC profile resembling that of AIIα, beginning with a broad endothermic region at 70 °C, followed by a minor endothermic peak (a) at 111 °C (marked with a brown circle) (ΔH = 55.9 J g−1), and a major melting peak (b) at 114 °C (ΔH = 11.05 J g−1), corresponding to the melting point of BI (Fig. 9a).

Starting from form BII, it undergoes partial desolvation and subsequent transformation into BI upon heating, thereby indicating conversion into the thermodynamically more stable form BI (Supplementary Table 15).
